title: Ojeda, Vespucci and de la Cosa along the Spanish Main, 1499
summary: Ojeda left Spain in May 1499 with four ships, with Juan de la Cosa as pilot and Amerigo Vespucci a passenger. He made landfall on the coast of Guiana, followed it west past Trinidad and Margarita, and found the Gulf of Venezuela, where houses on stilts over the water of Lake Maracaibo suggested Venice to them. They reached Hispaniola in September and went home with pearls and some captives.

events.label: Little Venice
events.text: In the Gulf of Venezuela they found villages on stilts, and called the country Venezuela, little Venice.
